clauses: Count each inventory copy as a film in stock.
Count each distinct film title with an inventory copy as a film in stock.
readings: Looking at the films we have in stock by `rating`, which ratings have more films in inventory than the average rating does? Give me a single row with the total films in stock across those above-average ratings and, on average, how far above the across-rating average they are (no rounding). Count each inventory copy as a film in stock.

Looking at the films we have in stock by `rating`, which ratings have more films in inventory than the average rating does? Give me a single row with the total films in stock across those above-average ratings and, on average, how far above the across-rating average they are (no rounding). Count each distinct film title with an inventory copy as a film in stock.
queries:
WITH rating_stock AS (
  SELECT f.rating, COUNT(*) AS films_in_stock
  FROM inventory AS i
  JOIN film AS f ON f.film_id = i.film_id
  GROUP BY f.rating
),
rating_average AS (
  SELECT AVG(films_in_stock) AS average_stock
  FROM rating_stock
)
SELECT
  SUM(rs.films_in_stock) AS total_films_in_stock,
  AVG(rs.films_in_stock - ra.average_stock) AS average_above_rating_average
FROM rating_stock AS rs
CROSS JOIN rating_average AS ra
WHERE rs.films_in_stock > ra.average_stock

WITH films_by_rating AS (
  SELECT f.rating, COUNT(DISTINCT f.title) AS films_in_stock
  FROM film AS f
  JOIN inventory AS i ON i.film_id = f.film_id
  GROUP BY f.rating
),
rating_average AS (
  SELECT AVG(films_in_stock) AS average_films
  FROM films_by_rating
)
SELECT
  SUM(f.films_in_stock) AS total_films_in_stock,
  AVG(f.films_in_stock - a.average_films) AS average_above_rating_average
FROM films_by_rating AS f
CROSS JOIN rating_average AS a
WHERE f.films_in_stock > a.average_films
